clue.text: Notice political party's unscripted comments

parts.note: a notice in a newspaper is an advertisement, shortened to ad
Lib is short for Liberal, the political party, so the Lib's gives the possessive letters

explanation.surface: A notice of the political party's off-the-cuff remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad libs are spontaneous remarks made without a prepared script.

clue.text: Took in story told by reading or writing workshop?

parts.note: to take in food is to eat, past tense ate
a story told can be a falsehood
reading and writing are two of the three Rs, so each can stand for R

explanation.surface: Someone who absorbed a story is told about a reading or writing workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, the basics of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or designer's studio is a creative workroom.

clue.text: Trainee pilots moving into left hand lock

indicators.note: the cadets move inside the other letters

parts.note: the ATC is the Air Training Corps, a British cadet organisation for young would-be fliers

explanation.surface: Trainee pilots move a left-hand lock.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATC is the Air Training Corps, a UK youth organisation linked to the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple fastening on a door or gate is a kind of catch.

clue.text: About brown mince, avoid odd bits like the plague

indicators.note: skipping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth and every even letter of the run

explanation.surface: A cook is told to avoid bits of mince as if they were plague-ridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like the plague' seems to say 'avoid at all costs' but is the definition: the Black Death was the bubonic plague.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Death was the classic form, marked by swollen lymph glands.

clue.text: Constant pressure here, I cry with a touch of rancour

parts.note: to sob is to cry

indicators.note: a touch of something is just a little of it, here only the opening letter of the word rancour

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to weeping bitterly under constant pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constant pressure here' is a definition by description: on a weather map these lines join places of equal pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather chart a line linking points of equal atmospheric pressure is so named.

clue.text: Brushes off edges of swish carpets

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: rugs are small carpets

explanation.surface: Brushes off the fringes of plush carpets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brushes' suggests a broom for the carpet; it is a verb of dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something casually is to shrug it off.

clue.text: Font's seen here in book — is it following appropriate lines?

indicators.note: following here means the words is and it come after the word for appropriate in the answer, though printed before it

parts.note: apt means appropriate
taken as written
it shortened to 't, as in 'tis
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A typographer asks whether a font follows lines in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Font' is a church basin, not typography; 'it' gives T as in the poetic 'tis.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptismal basin stands in the part of a church set aside for christening.

clue.text: Sign of deficiency in headless insects

indicators.note: headless means the opening letter is chopped off

parts.note: crickets are chirping insects

explanation.surface: Missing heads on insects suggest something is lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The bone disease of children results from a lack of vitamin D.

clue.text: Who knows a song by Debussy composed with only one bass part?

indicators.note: composed means made up anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a Debussy song was written with only one bass line.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has two Bs; 'with only one bass part' drops one B (bass) before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: When the outcome is uncertain, the phrase means nobody can say.

clue.text: Guys steady this explosive packed with earth

indicators.note: the explosive is filled or stuffed with the earth letter, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: TNT is the abbreviation for the explosive trinitrotoluene
E is the standard abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: Seems to describe steadying an explosive charge packed with soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' are the ropes that hold a camping shelter steady, not men.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes are the lines staked out to hold a canvas shelter upright.

clue.text: Ruin ends in penury — turn back from this

definitions.text: Ruin ends in penury — turn back from this

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, so the letters that follow are wrecked into a new order
the ends of a word are its first and last letters, here those of penury

explanation.surface: A warning that financial ruin ends in poverty, so retreat while you can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' reads as the definition but is the anagram signal; PY (first and last letters of 'penury') plus TURNBACK are shuffled. The whole clue then describes the state itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvency is a financial ruin that can leave someone in penury, a state to be avoided.

clue.text: Parts of garlic and henbane spliced, two plants in one

indicators.note: only parts of the two plant names are kept: garlic loses its opening three letters and henbane its closing four
spliced means joined end to end, so the two kept parts are run together

explanation.surface: A herbalist splices bits of garlic and henbane into one remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts of' keeps LIC from 'garlic' and HEN from 'henbane'. The definition is loose: this organism is a partnership of a fungus and an alga, neither strictly a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This growth is a symbiotic union of fungus and alga living as a single organism.

clue.text: With two feet cut, start to see about a doctor's instrument

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer letters go round the inner ones
cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: biped as an adjective means having two feet
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor, and the possessive adds the S

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of see

explanation.surface: A doctor's instrument, with an amputee starting to look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With two feet' reads as a description of the doctor but gives the adjective BIPED; 'cut' docks its last letter, and 'about' sets A GP inside after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind instrument with a bag and drones, played especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Uniform advice crossed out by returning journalist

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of crossed are rearranged
returning means the word for the journalist is read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Advice about a uniform is struck out by a journalist on her return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns CROSSED into DRESSCO; 'returning' turns ED into DE. 'crossed out' looks like one phrase meaning deleted.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules on what to wear amount to guidance about uniform dress.

clue.text: Psychoanalysis, perhaps, the result of pilfering?

definitions.text: Psychoanalysis, perhaps, the result of pilfering?

parts.words: Psychoanalysis, perhaps, the result of pilfering?
parts.note: an analyst is slangily called a shrink, so analysis is jokingly their era or business; shops also lose stock to theft under this name

explanation.walkthrough: Retailers use the term for stock lost to shoplifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops record stock lost to theft as a reduction in inventory.

clue.text: Greek characters fully satisfy on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror reverses, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sate is to satisfy completely

explanation.surface: Greek characters fully satisfy someone thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' seems to mean after thinking; it turns SATE round.
explanation.definitionFit: These are letters of the Greek alphabet, the seventh one in plural.

clue.text: Inside Holy Land?

indicators.note: only the inside of the word is kept, its first and last letters stripped away

parts.note: holy means sacred

explanation.surface: A question about something within the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a port in the Holy Land, so the surface is apt as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area, about 4,047 square metres, so a measure of ground.

clue.text: Infidel involved in armed robbery

parts.note: at means engaged in, as in 'at work'
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: An unbeliever takes part in an armed robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rejects belief in God is an unbeliever.

clue.text: Dinosaur's marrow to signify broken bone-setting?

indicators.note: marrow is the soft centre of a bone, so the middle letters of dinosaur are taken
broken means the letters of signify are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A palaeontologist mends a fossil bone using dinosaur marrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bone-setting' is not mending a fracture but setting into bone, turning to bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning into bone, as tissue hardens, is a playful sense of setting as bone.

clue.text: Island full of lots of bird dung and Australian lizards

indicators.note: the island abbreviation is filled with the other letters
lots of means most of, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: guano is seabird droppings

explanation.surface: An island full of bird droppings and Australian reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: These large tropical American reptiles are a family of lizard.

clue.text: Taunts mostly unnecessary

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: needless means unnecessary

explanation.surface: Insults are mostly pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: To goad or provoke someone is to needle them, as a verb.

clue.text: Fragrant shrub's attempt to climb up into flipping tree

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other
flipping means turned over, so the tree is read backwards

parts.note: an elm is a tree

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A fragrant shrub tries to climb a blasted tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but is the reversal signal on the tree; 'to climb up' reverses the attempt, read upward in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen with scented white flowers is a classic aromatic bush.

clue.text: Out, when unwell, without a tissue? Cheers

indicators.note: without in the old sense means outside, so the shuffled letters go round the other piece
a word that is unwell is out of sorts, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: a hanky is a handkerchief, a tissue for the nose

explanation.surface: Someone sneezing without a tissue is told to get out; cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when unwell' signals the anagram of 'Out', and 'without' in its old sense of outside wraps that round the tissue. 'without' tempts as meaning lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal British for an expression of gratitude.

clue.text: Result of troubles in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of result are stirred up

explanation.surface: Something is the outcome of the Troubles, the conflict in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Troubles were the decades of conflict in Northern Ireland; here the word 'troubles' only signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic province name is commonly used for the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Ghost from the underworld, the last to rise up

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means moving upward, so the final letter climbs to the top

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A ghost rises from the underworld, the last one up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the underworld' seems to describe the ghost; HADES is the fodder and its final S moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a spirit of the dead in classical myth, a phantom.

clue.text: Skilled worker — one in oil company at inception of two parties

indicators.note: at inception means the other piece comes at the beginning, ahead of the worker
in places the numeral inside the oil company abbreviation

parts.note: BP is the British oil company
one is the Roman numeral I
an artisan is a skilled craft worker

explanation.surface: A craftsman joins an oil firm right at the start of a cross-party venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Supported by or involving two political sides, as cooperation between rival groups.

clue.text: Maybe porter carrying Times wheels around this

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other piece inside it

parts.note: porter is a kind of dark beer, an example of ale
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A railway porter carries The Times past turning wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' and 'Times' suggest a station worker with a newspaper; they are the beer and the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheels spin on the rod or shaft that joins them.

clue.text: 2 letters or 9?

parts.note: the twentieth letter of the alphabet written out as a word
the sixteenth letter of the alphabet written out as a word

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether two letters of the alphabet could stand for a camping shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2 letters are T and P spelled as words; '9' points to the answer at 9 across, of which this is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical tent used by Plains peoples of North America is one kind of the canvas shelter at 9.

clue.text: They show way to remove power from drug dealers

indicators.note: remove means the power letter is taken out of the dealers

parts.note: pushers are people who sell illegal drugs
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Seems to tell police how to get rid of drug dealers' power.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre or wedding attendants guide people to their seats.
